title: Exercise 4 – Smooth Operator SA
text: Smooth Operator SA is a listed firm with a market capitalization of EUR 100 billion, EUR 50 billion of debt outstanding, and no excess cash. The expected return on its equity is 8%. The risk-free rate is 2% and the expected market return is 6%. Assume perfect capital markets.

title: Exercise 5 – Club Med's leveraged recapitalization
text: The Chief Financial Officer of Club Med is analyzing the impact of a leveraged recapitalization on the firm's value. Club Med is currently all-equity financed: its equity is worth EUR 8 billion and its (unlevered) cost of capital is 9%. The firm plans to issue EUR 2 billion worth of perpetual bonds and to use the proceeds to repurchase EUR 2 billion worth of equity. The bonds are risk-free with an annual interest rate of 5%. Assume perfect capital markets (no taxes, no costs of financial distress).
In the original paper this exercise is on the interest tax shield, which is not part of lectures 1–8; it is rebuilt here for a perfect capital market.

title: Exercise 6 – Ghost Writer
text: Ghost Writer is a software company that specializes in detecting AI-generated content. Its shares trade at EUR 60 today. Analysts expect a share price of EUR 64 in one year and a dividend of EUR 1 per share at that date. Ghost Writer's equity beta is 1.3, the risk-free rate is 2% and the expected market return is 6%.
In the original paper this exercise is on an IPO auction, which is not part of lectures 1–8.
